theory.title: Exercise 4.3.4: Convert Date
theory.content:
MENTOR-9: "External systems use different date formats. APIs return ISO, logs use custom formats, users enter dates their way. Convert Date handles all conversions."

Convert Date

Parse and reformat dates:

Library    DateTime

# Parse US format, output ISO
${date}=    Convert Date    10/04/2025 02:30 PM
    ...    date_format=%m/%d/%Y %I:%M %p
    ...    result_format=%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S
# Result: 2025-10-04 14:30:00

# Parse European, output custom
${date}=    Convert Date    04.10.2025
    ...    date_format=%d.%m.%Y
    ...    result_format=%B %d, %Y
# Result: October 04, 2025

Common Format Codes:

  • %Y: 4-digit year
  • %m: Month number (01-12)
  • %d: Day (01-31)
  • %H: Hour 24h (00-23)
  • %I: Hour 12h (01-12)
  • %M: Minute (00-59)
  • %S: Second (00-59)
  • %p: AM/PM
  • %B: Full month name

Example: Normalize Log Timestamps

*** Settings ***
Library    DateTime

*** Test Cases ***
Normalize Timestamps
    @{logs}=    Create List    10/04/2025 14:30    04.10.2025 14:30    2025-10-04 14:30
    @{normalized}=    Create List
    FOR    ${log}    IN    @{logs}
        TRY
            ${norm}=    Convert Date    ${log}    result_format=%Y-%m-%d %H:%M
            Append To List    ${normalized}    ${norm}
        EXCEPT
            # Try different format
            ${norm}=    Convert Date    ${log}    date_format=%d.%m.%Y %H:%M    result_format=%Y-%m-%d %H:%M
            Append To List    ${normalized}    ${norm}
        END
    END

⚠️ Convert Date Tips

  • date_format: How to parse input
  • result_format: How to format output
  • If input is ISO 8601, date_format optional
  • Use for: format normalization, parsing logs, API integration
  • Combine with TRY/EXCEPT for format auto-detection
